goldens.comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No error handling on findMembers() promise in routes - AJAX failures are silently swallowed with no user feedback

adjudication.rationale: In both `admin_group_route.js` and `discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6`, the diff removes the prior `afterModel` hook that returned `model.findMembers().then(...)` and replaces it with a bare `model.findMembers();` call inside `setupController` without returning the promise or attaching a `.catch(...)`. Since `findMembers()` performs `Discourse.ajax(...)` and returns its promise, any AJAX rejection will no longer participate in the route transition’s promise chain (so Ember’s route error handling won’t trigger), and there is no explicit error handling/user feedback added. This is a concrete behavioral regression introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addMembers action doesn't clear the input field after adding members, risking duplicate add attempts or confusion

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the `addMembers` action calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"));` but never resets/clears the bound `usernames` property afterward. The template binds `{{user-selector usernames=usernames ...}}`, so the input will retain the entered usernames after adding. The code even includes a `// TODO: should clear the input` comment, confirming the behavior is currently missing and could lead to accidental repeated submissions/confusion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No tests for the public members endpoint changes - response format changed from serialized array to { members: [...], meta: {...} }, pagination logic is untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the public `GroupsController#members` response from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (an array) to a JSON object with `{ members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }` and adds limit/offset behavior for all groups. In the same diff, only `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb` is modified/added; there are no corresponding specs added/updated for `GroupsController#members` to assert the new response shape or pagination/meta semantics. So the finding about missing tests for this endpoint change is verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: group.users.delete(user_id) passes an integer id to collection delete which is non-idiomatic and potentially fragile across Rails versions
members property not declared on the Group model despite being set via setProperties, risking improper KVO notification in Ember 1.x

adjudication.rationale: In Ember 1.x, calling `set`/`setProperties` on an `Ember.Object` (or `Discourse.Model` which extends it) defines the property if it doesn’t already exist and triggers the normal property change notifications. In the diff, `findMembers()` does `self.setProperties({ ... members: ... })`, which will create/update `members` and notify bindings/templates. Ember does not require pre-declaring `members` on the model for KVO to work, so the stated “risking improper KVO notification” is not a verifiable defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silent failure for non-existent usernames in add_members - misspelled usernames are skipped with no error or user feedback

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the code iterates `usernames.split(",")` and only adds a user if `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a record. Non-existent/misspelled usernames are simply skipped (no error collection), and the action still returns `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds. There is no response indicating which usernames failed, so the client will see a success despite some additions being ignored.
